reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) supports the clustering-to-ordering transition under high-strain compression and the retention of clustering under tension, but provides no evidence linking chemical ordering to electron–phonon coupling or superconducting properties. The key mechanistic premises about superconductivity are entirely unsupported.
premises: High-strain compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi
This transition occurs at elevated temperatures (300–500 °C)
Tensile loading and annealing retain a clustered state
Increased chemical ordering modulates electron–phonon coupling
Modulated electron–phonon coupling alters superconducting properties (Tc, gap)
